Notation. M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, μ := V.weight = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal ∘ θ, so that μ(S) = ∫_{S∩M} θ dHⁿ for Borel S; ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n]. The contract's structure fields give: M ⊆ U, M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is AE-measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U.

Proof.
1. Compact exhaustion of U. For i ∈ ℕ let Q_i := {x : |x| ≤ i and Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ ≥ 1/(i + 1)} (with infEDist x ∅ = ∞). Q_i is closed (Metric.continuous_infEDist) and bounded, hence compact. Q_i ⊆ U, since x ∉ U means x ∈ Uᶜ and then infEDist x Uᶜ = 0. ⋃_i Q_i = U: for x ∈ U, x ∉ closure(Uᶜ) = Uᶜ, so infEDist x Uᶜ > 0 (Metric.infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure), and both defining conditions hold for all large i.
2. A Borel good part of M. Let θ̃ be a Borel function with θ = θ̃ (Hⁿ⌞M)-almost everywhere (aemeasurable_mult.mk). As M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, Hⁿ(M ∩ {θ ≠ θ̃}) = 0. Choose a Borel M' ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ M') = 0 (nullMeasurableSet_carrier with NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq) and a Borel Hⁿ-null set T ⊇ M ∩ {θ ≠ θ̃} (toMeasurable), and set M'' := M' ∖ T. Then M'' is Borel, M'' ⊆ M, θ = θ̃ on M'', and Hⁿ(M ∖ M'') = 0.
3. Finite measures. μ(Q_i) = ∫_{M∩Q_i} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by integrableOn_mult (Q_i is compact and Q_i ⊆ U). So ν_i := μ⌞Q_i is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence weakly regular (MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure): every Borel set of finite ν_i-measure contains closed subsets of almost full measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt).
4. Lusin. For i, m ∈ ℕ apply SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (Simon 1.17) with ν = ν_i, the Borel set A_i := M'' ∩ Q_i (ν_i(A_i) < ∞), the Borel function θ̃ and ε = 1/(m + 1): there is a closed C_{i,m} ⊆ A_i with ν_i(A_i ∖ C_{i,m}) < 1/(m + 1) on which θ̃ is continuous.
5. Properties of C_{i,m}. It is compact (a closed subset of the compact Q_i), and C_{i,m} ⊆ M'' ⊆ M. Since θ = θ̃ on C_{i,m}, θ is continuous on C_{i,m}. If C_{i,m} ≠ ∅, θ is continuous and positive on the compact C_{i,m}, so θ ≥ c > 0 there (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn) and c·Hⁿ(C_{i,m}) ≤ ∫_{C_{i,m}} θ dHⁿ = μ(C_{i,m}) ≤ μ(Q_i) < ∞; hence Hⁿ(C_{i,m}) < ∞ (trivially also when C_{i,m} = ∅).
6. Null remainder. S_i := A_i ∖ ⋃_m C_{i,m} is Borel with S_i ⊆ M ∩ Q_i, and μ(S_i) = ν_i(S_i) ≤ ν_i(A_i ∖ C_{i,m}) < 1/(m + 1) for every m, so 0 = μ(S_i) = ∫_{S_i} ofReal ∘ θ dHⁿ. Since θ > 0 on S_i, this forces Hⁿ(S_i) = 0 (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). Because M ⊆ U = ⋃_i Q_i, every x ∈ M'' lies in some A_i, so M ∖ ⋃_{i,m} C_{i,m} ⊆ (M ∖ M'') ∪ ⋃_i S_i, which is Hⁿ-null.
7. Enumeration. Let K_k := C_{i,m} where (i, m) := Nat.unpair k. Each K_k is compact, K_k ⊆ M, θ is continuous on K_k, Hⁿ(K_k) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k K_k) = 0. ∎

Source: Simon, Ch. 2, printed proof of Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem: Rademacher, Lusin, Egoroff, Whitney extension 1.6), with details filled in. The book's remarks that Lusin's theorem 'applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ' and that Egoroff is applied 'to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0)' with uniform convergence 'on each bounded subset' are implemented below by working on the open annuli Ann_j.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume; |·| is the Euclidean norm; B_r(x) is the closed ball and B°_r(x) the open ball. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) (this is 0 where f is not differentiable).

Proof.
0. Reductions. Replacing ε by min(ε, 1) we may assume that 0 < ε ≤ 1 is a real number. For j ∈ ℕ let Ann_j := {x : j < |x| < j + 1} (open and bounded) and ε_j := ε·2^(−j−3), so that Σ_j ε_j = ε/4. Every x with |x| ∉ ℕ lies in exactly one Ann_j, and each sphere {|x| = j} is Lⁿ-null because n ≥ 1 (Measure.addHaar_sphere). Df is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv), so are its components x ↦ Df(x)e_i, i = 1, …, n (measurable_fderiv_apply_const), and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ K for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
1. Rademacher. B := {x : f is differentiable at x} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0 (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt).
2. Lusin on annuli. Fix j and let S_j := Ann_j ∩ B, a Borel set of finite measure. Lebesgue measure is regular, so every Borel set of finite measure contains closed subsets of almost full measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt); this is the regularity hypothesis of SimonGMT's finite-measure Lusin theorem Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable. Applying it with ν = volume and A = S_j to each component x ↦ Df(x)e_i with tolerance ε_j/n gives closed sets C_{j,i} ⊆ S_j with Lⁿ(S_j ∖ C_{j,i}) < ε_j/n such that x ↦ Df(x)e_i is continuous on C_{j,i}. Put C_j := ⋂_{i=1}^n C_{j,i}. Then C_j is closed, C_j ⊆ S_j, Lⁿ(S_j ∖ C_j) < ε_j, and Df is continuous on C_j (continuousOn_clm_apply: a map into L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is continuous on a set iff all its evaluations are). C_j is compact and contained in the open annulus Ann_j, hence there is δ_j > 0 with j + δ_j ≤ |x| ≤ j + 1 − δ_j for all x ∈ C_j.
3. Gluing. Let C := ⋃_j C_j. Every point of ℝⁿ has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many Ann_j, hence only finitely many C_j; so the family (C_j) is locally finite and C is closed (LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion). If x ∈ C_j, then B°_{δ_j}(x) ∩ C = B°_{δ_j}(x) ∩ C_j, because the points of B°_{δ_j}(x) have norm in (j, j + 1); hence Df restricted to C is continuous at x. Moreover C ⊆ B, and ℝⁿ ∖ C ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ B) ∪ ⋃_j {|x| = j} ∪ ⋃_j (S_j ∖ C_j), so Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ 0 + 0 + Σ_j ε_j = ε/4.
4. Whitney quotients. For x ≠ y set R(x, y) := (f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x))/|y − x|. For k ≥ 1 define σ_k(x) := sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} for x ∈ C (with sup ∅ := 0), and σ_k(x) := 0 for x ∉ C.
 (a) 0 ≤ σ_k ≤ 2K, because |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ K|y − x| and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ K.
 (b) σ_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞ for every x ∈ C: since x ∈ B, for every η > 0 there is δ > 0 with |R(x, y)| ≤ η whenever 0 < |y − x| < δ, so σ_k(x) ≤ η as soon as 1/k ≤ δ.
 (c) σ_k is Borel measurable. Let D₀ ⊆ C be countable and dense in C (C is a separable metric space; TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). For fixed x, the map y ↦ R(x, y) is continuous on ℝⁿ ∖ {x} (f is continuous), and {y ∈ C : 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, hence D₀ is dense in it; therefore σ_k(x) = sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ D₀, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} for x ∈ C. For each fixed y ∈ D₀ the function x ↦ 1_C(x)·1_{0<|y−x|<1/k}(x)·|R(x, y)| is Borel (f continuous, Df Borel, indicators of Borel sets). Hence σ_k is a countable supremum of Borel functions bounded by 2K, so it is Borel measurable and strongly measurable.
5. Egorov and inner regularity. Fix j. C_j is Borel of finite measure, every σ_k is strongly measurable, and σ_k → 0 at every point of C_j. By Egorov's theorem (MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) there is a Borel t_j ⊆ C_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε_j such that σ_k → 0 uniformly on A'_j := C_j ∖ t_j. By inner regularity choose a closed A_j ⊆ A'_j with Lⁿ(A'_j ∖ A_j) < ε_j; A_j is compact and A_j ⊆ C_j ⊆ Ann_j. Let A := ⋃_j A_j. As in step 3 the family (A_j) is locally finite, so A is closed; A ⊆ C; and since ℝⁿ ∖ A ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ C) ∪ ⋃_j (t_j ∪ (A'_j ∖ A_j)), we get Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ ε/4 + Σ_j ε_j + Σ_j ε_j = 3ε/4 < ε. Finally, a compact Q ⊆ A is contained in B_J(0) for some J ∈ ℕ, hence in A_0 ∪ … ∪ A_J; therefore σ_k → 0 uniformly on Q.
6. Whitney's hypothesis 1.6(*). We verify SimonGMT's structure Chapter02.HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df. (continuous_value) f is continuous on A. (continuous_derivative) Df is continuous on A, since A ⊆ C (step 3). (remainder) Given a compact Q ⊆ A and η > 0, choose k with σ_k ≤ η on Q (step 5) and put δ := 1/k. For x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ, either y = x (and the remainder vanishes) or y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, so |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| = |R(x, y)|·|y − x| ≤ σ_k(x)|y − x| ≤ η|y − x|.
7. Whitney extension (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney, applicable since A is closed) yields g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 g and g = f on A. Then {x : f(x) ≠ g(x)} ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ A, so Lⁿ({f ≠ g}) < ε. ∎

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^{n+ℓ}. It is the translation z ↦ z − x followed by the dilation w ↦ r⁻¹w (r⁻¹ ≠ 0), with continuous inverse y ↦ x + r y. Hence η is a bijection and a Borel measurable equivalence, in particular a measurable embedding.
   Lean: e := (Homeomorph.subRight x).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero hr.ne')). This is definitionally Chapter03.blowUpMap x r (`fun z => rfl`). Take E := e.toMeasurableEquiv.

2. Scaling. For every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, measurable or not, Hⁿ(η(S)) = (r⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(S).
   - η(S) = h(τ(S)), where τ(y) = y − x and h is the homothety with centre 0 and ratio r⁻¹.
   - τ is an isometry: dist(a − x, b − x) = ‖a − b‖. So Hⁿ(τ(S)) = Hⁿ(S) by Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image.
   - Images under h have μHE[n]-measure multiplied by ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), and ‖r⁻¹‖ = r⁻¹ because r > 0.
   In [0,∞] the factor is c := ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ, which is finite and positive.

3. Restricted measures. Claim: Hⁿ⌞η(M) = c·η_#(Hⁿ⌞M). It suffices to compare the two measures on Borel sets A (Measure.ext).

   - Since η⁻¹(A) is Borel, Hⁿ(η⁻¹(A) ∩ M) = (Hⁿ⌞M)(η⁻¹(A)) = (η_#(Hⁿ⌞M))(A) (Measure.restrict_apply, Measure.map_apply).
   Measure.restrict_apply only requires the evaluated set to be measurable, never the restricting set, so measurability of M is not used.

   - Finally c.toReal = (r⁻¹)ⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ (ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, inv_pow).

3. Change of variables (H1). For λ > 0, every function g and every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}:
 ∫_{η_λ(S)} g(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n) ∫_S g(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z),
 because the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞η_λ(S) under the homeomorphism y ↦ x + λy equals λ^(−n)·Hⁿ⌞S (SimonGMT Chapter04.map_inverse_blowUp_carrier, with Chapter04.blowUpHomeomorph), followed by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure; this identity of Bochner integrals requires no integrability. The same identity holds with θ replaced by the constant 1.
4. Splitting. Fix f ∈ C_c, R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), M_f := sup|f|, and 0 < λ < ρ/R. The function h_λ(z) := f(η_λ(z))θ(z) vanishes for z ∉ B_{λR}(x), and |h_λ| ≤ M_f·θ on M ∩ B_{λR}(x) ⊆ M ∩ B_ρ(x); h_λ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M; hence h_λ is integrable on M. Writing M as the disjoint union of the Borel set K and M ∖ K, and θ(z) = θ(x) + (θ(z) − θ(x)) on K, step 3 gives
 ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n)∫_M h_λ dHⁿ = I_1 + I_2 + I_3, where
 I_1 := θ(x)·λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z)) dHⁿ(z) = θ(x)∫_{η_λ(K)} f dHⁿ,
 I_2 := λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z))(θ(z) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(z),
 I_3 := λ^(−n)∫_{M∖K} f(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z);
 all three integrands are integrable (bounded by multiples of 1_K or of θ·1_{M ∩ B_ρ(x)}, using Hⁿ(K) < ∞ and step 2).
5. I_1 → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ, by T_xK = P.
6. I_3 → 0. |I_3| ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)∫_{(M∖K) ∩ B_{λR}(x)} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)·μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)), because ∫_S ofReal ∘ θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) ≤ μ(S) for every set S (withDensity_apply_le) and θ > 0 on M. By hypothesis μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))/ofReal(λⁿ) → 0 in [0, ∞]; hence it is finite for small λ and its real value tends to 0. So I_3 → 0.
7. I_2 → 0. Let ω(s) := sup{|θ(z) − θ(x)| : z ∈ K ∩ B_s(x)}; ω(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 because θ restricted to K is continuous at x. Then |I_2| ≤ M_f·ω(λR)·λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)). The last factor stays bounded (Remark 1.5(3)): λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = Hⁿ(η_λ(K) ∩ B_R(0)) (SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_ball) ≤ ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ, where g(y) := min{1, max{0, 2 − |y|/R}} is in C_c with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g = 1 on B_R(0); and ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ → ∫_P g dHⁿ < ∞ by T_xK = P. Hence the last factor is bounded for small λ and I_2 → 0.
8. By steps 4–7, ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c; together with step 1 this is W(x, P). ∎

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n and ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces; L† := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L; p_S := S.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto a subspace S; End(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ is a complete normed ring; Ring.inverse is the inverse on units and 0 elsewhere.

Proof.
1. The set 𝓘 := {L : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^{n+ℓ} | L injective} is open (ContinuousLinearMap.isOpen_injective; ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional).
2. For L ∈ 𝓘 let A_L := L† ∘ L ∈ End(ℝⁿ). For v ≠ 0, ⟨A_L v, v⟩ = ⟨Lv, Lv⟩ = |Lv|² > 0, so A_L is injective, hence bijective (finite dimension), hence a unit of End(ℝⁿ).
3. Define Q_L := L ∘ Ring.inverse(A_L) ∘ L† : ℝ^{n+ℓ} →L[ℝ] ℝ^{n+ℓ}. For L ∈ 𝓘 and w ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}: Q_L w = L(A_L^(−1) L† w) ∈ L(ℝⁿ), and for every v ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨w − Q_L w, Lv⟩ = ⟨L†w − L†L A_L^(−1) L†w, v⟩ = ⟨L†w − L†w, v⟩ = 0. So w − Q_L w is orthogonal to L(ℝⁿ), and Q_L w = p_{L(ℝⁿ)} w (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Thus Q_L = p_{L(ℝⁿ)} for all L ∈ 𝓘.
4. Continuity of Q at L₀ ∈ 𝓘. L ↦ L† is continuous (the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence), and composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, so L ↦ A_L is continuous. Ring.inverse is continuous at the unit A_{L₀} (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). Hence L ↦ Q_L = L ∘ Ring.inverse(A_L) ∘ L† is continuous at L₀.
5. For L₀ ∈ 𝓘, the map L ↦ p_{L(ℝⁿ)} agrees with Q on 𝓘 and Q is continuous at L₀, so L ↦ p_{L(ℝⁿ)} is continuous within 𝓘 at L₀ (ContinuousAt.continuousWithinAt and ContinuousWithinAt.congr, using p_{L₀(ℝⁿ)} = Q_{L₀}). Hence the map is ContinuousOn 𝓘. ∎
